articles.title: Reuters Institute Survey Shows ChatGPT Use Is Broad, but Daily Habits Remain Limited
articles.summary: ChatGPT is the most widely used generative AI tool in a six-country Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism survey, but the data also show a clear gap between trying the technology and making it part of a daily routine. Across Argentina, Denmark, France, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States, 22% of respondents reported using ChatGPT weekly on average. Daily use was substantially lower. That distinction matters for businesses assessing AI adoption. A large number of people may be familiar with ChatGPT, yet frequent use is not universal. The survey's central lesson is not simply that generative AI has reached a broad audience. It is that sustained, habitual use still depends on whether people can find useful, repeatable roles for it. The figures come from the Reuters Institute's analysis of public attitudes to generative AI in six countries. articles.title: How the AI ROI Gap Comes Down to Trust
articles.summary: Companies investing in trustworthy AI practices are far more likely to see strong returns from the technology, according to new research from SAS. But trust remains a hurdle: 97% of users override AI recommendations at least some of the time, while employees are less likely to trust increasingly autonomous AI agents. Jay Upchurch, SAS Executive Vice President and Chief Information Officer, joins Bloomberg's Anna Edwards on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
